analysis.evidence: לָהֶם נָשִׁים means “wives for themselves.” The verse then names Sarai as Abram’s wife and Milcah as Nahor’s wife, confirming the marriage sense.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol in the third person masculine singular. The singular verb precedes the compound subject Abram and Nahor.

analysis.evidence: אַבְרָם and וְנָחוֹר form the compound subject of וַיִּקַּח. The verse then identifies Sarai as Abram’s wife.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: Abram and Nahor take wives. The phrase שֵׁם אֵשֶׁת נָחוֹר מִלְכָּה identifies Milcah as the wife of this Nahor.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ joins the personal name נָחוֹר to אַבְרָם. Together the two names form the subject of וַיִּקַּח.
analysis.sense: Nahor, Abram’s brother and Milcah’s husband

analysis.evidence: In שֵׁם אֵשֶׁת אַבְרָם שָׂרָי, שָׂרָי supplies the name of Abram’s wife. The parallel clause gives Milcah as the name of Nahor’s wife.

analysis.evidence: The verse says that Abram and Nahor took wives. The phrase שֵׁם אֵשֶׁת אַבְרָם שָׂרָי then identifies Sarai as Abram’s wife.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state. The following name אַבְרָם identifies whose wife she is.
